newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - March 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Senate will look into the alleged funding problem besetting the May 12 town elections amid charges that it was orchestrated by the Palace. (TODAY/STANDARD/CHRONICLE)

- Speaker Jose de Venecia hosts a crucial breakfast meeting today with Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo, Executive Secrteray Ruben Torres and leaders of the House ways and means committee to draw up a compromise on the exemption level for income taxes. (JOURNAL/INQUIRER)
- A brother of Las Pinas town mayor Vergel Aguilar was abducted by six heavily armed men on the Alabang-Zapote road on Monday morning. (MALAYA)

- The price cuts implemented yesterday by the three oil firms were substantially lower than the average Singapore posted prices during the base period of February 6 to March 6, industrialist Raul Concepcion, chairman of the Oil Price Watch, said yesterday. (INQUIRER/JOURNAL)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission has withheld further action on the application of the Philippine Stock Exchange for a permanent self-regulatory organisation status until the bourse has named a suitable replacement for resigned president Vitaliano Nanagas. (INQUIRER/TODAY)

- Cash-strapped Victorias Milling Corp will call on existing shareholders for additional capital and reduce personnel as a means of raising funds to pay the 4.4 billion pesos it owes 32 banks. (MALAYA/TIMES/CHRONICLE)
